cases.question: why was every module of every crate open?
cases.answer: the import fixed point never settled: a period-4 oscillation from order-dependent visibility (src/ast/mod.rs `use crate::*;` then `pub use expr::*;`) and a registry path growing one segment per round (`use quote::quote;` resolving its first segment through itself); the resolver iterates the workspace as one state, so the 64-round fallback opened all of it

cases.question: what did settling expose?
cases.answer: calls of the crate's own EGraph claimed external: `extern crate self as egglog;` bound its item to an external root, and `use crate::*; pub use egglog::{EGraph, ..};` passed that on. Fixed in the same epoch; then two review passes found five more holes (four WRONG-claim classes, one 57x slowdown), all closed (ADR 0091)

cases.question: are the new external paths right?
cases.answer: 417 open-scope calls became external paths; 322 are confirmed external by the index; the rest are the trait-path convention (`Default::default` names core's trait method, the index names the impl) or standard calls where the index's first occurrence is a workspace symbol among the arguments; none names workspace code

implementation.mechanism_vs_implementation: nothing of egglog is absorbed: its workspace, indexed by rust-analyzer, exposed that Atlas's import fixed point could fail to converge on code rustc accepts; the fix follows rustc's own name-resolution rules (try_define keeps the more visible of two bindings of one item; ignore_import; extern crate items; the namespaces an import binds), not any egglog code
implementation.change: adapter semantic::rust::resolve: DefMap::covers/bind (same-origin bindings keep the wider visibility, merged unsure bindings keep both sides), import_prefix/own_named (an import never reads its own binding, one name looked up), the fallback distrusts named imports, extern_items/bind_extern_crates/crate_named (an extern crate item names its crate), Entry.unsure and either (an external import may bind nothing in a namespace), STD_CRATE_NAMED, restricted_to (pub(in path)), glob visibility the narrower of import and item; CrateInput.declared and runtime crate_targets_locked (every declared dependency name); adapter dependency::cargo ManifestTargets.lib_name; adapter dependency::cargo: a native TOML reader (every string kind, full key paths, unreadable entries declared but unbound); runtime: an extern name is the one Cargo passes (the library's crate name unless renamed), an empty path, an unseen workspace root or conflicting entries bind nothing
implementation.falsification: regression tests one_item_through_two_globs_keeps_the_wider_visibility, an_import_never_resolves_its_path_through_its_own_binding, without_a_fixed_point_no_named_import_is_trusted, an_extern_crate_item_binds_the_crate_it_names, one per review hole, and every_declared_dependency_names_the_extern_prelude_whatever_its_source; 88 mutants killed
implementation.review: four independent adversarial passes, each reproduced on rustc 1.90.0 or Cargo: (1) an external import bound in both namespaces rooted alloc:: paths at the function (WRONG), a quadratic self-excluding lookup (57x), glob re-exports and pub(in path) read too wide (older); (2) a value-only std import beside a dependency the lockfile does not confirm claimed the std path and a workspace method (older, WRONG), and an order-dependent merge; (3) workspace dependencies keyed by manifest key instead of library name (older, WRONG) and manifest spellings that dropped dependencies; (4) by differential against tomllib over 636 registry manifests and generated corpora, a triple-quoted path read as empty (introduced by the third fix, WRONG) and five older reader holes -- the line reader replaced by a native TOML reader, then 0 wrong, dropped or extra entries over 12,734 manifests
